paper.title: Analytic reproducibility in articles receiving open data badges at the journal Psychological Science: an observational study

findings.evidence: The paper reports 'percent articles reproducible with author involvement' = 34 % (Abstract); the authors' own stored output (bp_work/results/manuscript.tex) gives 24. Our re-run gives 24, which matches the stored output.
'n checked values' is reported with different values. Abstract: 789 values | Results p.4: 879 values. Agreeing reports: 1 location(s) [Abstract] vs 1 [Results p.4].

findings.location: Abstract vs Table 1 (row 'yes / with author involvement')
findings.evidence: Abstract: 'reproducible with author involvement for 6 (34% [8,47]) articles'. Table 1 and Results: 6 (24%, [8,47]). 6/25 = 24%; the stored output (results/manuscript.tex, Table 1) prints 24%. The 34% in the Abstract is the only place with 34%. [Red (build_passport.py, archive_verified): the verification stage printed the authors' stored value with an executed check and upheld the conflict.]

findings.location: Abstract vs Results p.4 vs Sample p.3
findings.evidence: Abstract: '37 major numerical discrepancies remained out of 789 checked values (5% [3,6])'. Results p.4: '37 major numerical discrepancies remained among the 879 target values examined'. Sample p.3: '789 discrete numerical values ... were designated as target values'. data_values.csv has 789 rows and the stored output prints 789; 37/789 = 4.7% -> 5%, 37/879 = 4.2% -> 4%. [Red (build_passport.py, archive_verified): the verification stage printed the authors' stored value with an executed check and upheld the conflict.]

Sample p.3: '789 discrete numerical values reported in 27 articles ... were designated as target values', but data_articles.csv has 25 rows and the paper elsewhere reports 25 articles throughout (Abstract, Results, Table 1). The 27 is not explained by any exclusion step in the text.

findings.location: Results p.4 ('A comparison sample of 30 articles from the same journal without open data badges')
findings.evidence: The comparison sample of 30 articles (21 with >=1 major discrepancy, 70%) is described in the Results, but the materials contain no data file, code or supplementary item for it: data/raw holds only data_values.csv (789 rows, 25 articles), data_articles.csv (25 rows), Kidwell and Hardwicke2018 files; no 30-article file and no code computing 21/30.
